classification.difficultyReason: Find the height above eye level using tangent, then add the observer's eye height.

content.prompt:
From a point $20\text{ m}$ from the base of a tree, Sophia measures the angle of elevation of the top of the tree to be $39^\circ$. Her eye level is $1.64\text{ m}$ above the ground.
Calculate the height of the tree in metres correct to two decimal places.

spec.description: Observer left and outline tree right. Dashed horizontal, vertical and line of sight form the triangle. The vertical dimension d runs from eye level to the tree top, not from the ground. Context illustrations are simplified to editable black outlines without decorative fills.
spec.mathematics: Horizontal distance 20 m; eye height 1.64 m; angle of elevation 39 degrees; d = 20 tan(39 degrees); total tree height = d + 1.64 m.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown d are visible; no calculated heights appear.
